scenario: Alterion 技术面，面试官问「读多的数据库怎么扩」。你想说读写分离，却说成 separate the read pass and the write pass，还卡在 we want to consistency。
scenario_en: In an Alterion technical interview you're asked how to scale a read-heavy database. You mean read/write separation but say "separate the read pass and the write pass" and stall on "we want to consistency."
q: 「读写分离」这句话，工程师会怎么说出口？
q_en: How does an engineer actually say "read/write separation" out loud?
options: I would separate the read pass and the write pass, so, so if we want it to be consistent...
so we send the reads to one place and the writes to another place, the read one is kind of a copy...
I'd split the read path from the write path — reads hit a replica, writes go to the primary.
The system shall segregate read operations from write operations across separate database nodes.
tradeoff: 地道术语 vs 直译卡壳：path 加 hit a replica 一句证明你懂机制；read pass 和 we want to consistency 是词形错加语法崩，听着像没吃透。
why: 术语是 read path，不是 read pass；读走 replica、写走 primary 一句点明机制。consistency 前别接 to be。
why_en: It's the read path and the write path — reads hit a replica, writes go to the primary.
whenOtherWins: 只有给非技术的人解释时才用 one place 大白话，正式面试要 path、replica、primary。
options_en: I would separate the read pass and the write pass, so, so if we want it to be consistent...
so we send the reads to one place and the writes to another place, the read one is kind of a copy...
I'd split the read path from the write path — reads hit a replica, writes go to the primary.
The system shall segregate read operations from write operations across separate database nodes.
optionMeanings: 原话把 path 说成 pass，还接错语法。
把副本主库说成 place、copy，边说边打转。
术语准确，点明读走副本、写走主库。
书面公文腔，像念规范文档。
optionMeanings_en: Precise terms: reads to replica, writes to primary.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方以为你没真做过读写分离。
全程模糊，拼不出流量怎么分。
对方立刻懂你的分流方案。
过度正式，像背文档不像讨论。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They doubt you've really done this.
All vague — can't see how traffic splits.
They instantly get your split.
Over-formal — a doc, not a chat.
optionDirectness: 错在词形：path 说成 pass。
错在粒度：只泛指，没点副本主库。
抓住 read/write path 加副本主库机制。
错在语域：书面体太僵。
optionDirectness_en: Nails read/write path with the mechanism.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读请求走的那条链路；扩读多的系统就是把它引到副本上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The read path is the route a read request takes; you scale reads by sending it to a replica.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写请求走的那条链路；写通常只落到主库保证一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The write path is the route a write takes; writes usually go only to the primary.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主库数据的一份副本，专门分担读流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A replica is a copy of the primary's data that serves read traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 接收所有写入的主库，副本从它同步数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The primary is the database that takes all writes; replicas sync from it.

scenario: 系统设计面，面试官追问「主库挂了会怎样」。你知道要切到副本，但一开口就说成 the main one is dead、do a failover 这类怪词形。
scenario_en: In a system design round the interviewer asks, "What happens when the primary DB dies?" You know you switch to a replica, but out come odd forms like "the main one is dead" and "do a failover."
q: 「主库故障、切换到备库」这句话怎么说才地道？
q_en: How do you naturally say "the primary fails, we switch to the standby"?
options: If the primary goes down, we fail over to a standby replica and promote it to primary.
if the main one is dead, we do a failover to make the copy the main one, the failover happen fast...
so if it dies, we, we switch to another one, so that other one becomes the, the main one, yeah...
Upon primary node failure, an automated failover procedure promotes a replica to primary.
tradeoff: 动词 fail over vs 名词乱用：动作链地道紧凑；the main one 加 do a failover 词形松散，听着像外行转述。
why: 动作用动词 fail over，再 promote 副本当 primary；名词 failover 别当动词。primary 比 the main one 专业。
why_en: We fail over to a standby replica and promote it to primary — "fail over" is the verb.
whenOtherWins: 只有给非技术同事讲流程时，switch to another one 才够；面试要 fail over、promote、primary。
options_en: If the primary goes down, we fail over to a standby replica and promote it to primary.
if the main one is dead, we do a failover to make the copy the main one, the failover happen fast...
so if it dies, we, we switch to another one, so that other one becomes the, the main one, yeah...
Upon primary node failure, an automated failover procedure promotes a replica to primary.
optionMeanings: 动词形加提升副本，术语链紧凑。
把 failover 当动词，还说 the main one。
全程 switch，卡在主库称呼打转。
公文腔，像念故障预案。
optionMeanings_en: Verb form plus promoting a replica — tight.
Uses failover as a verb, says "the main one."
All "switch," stuck on naming the primary.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方知道你懂切换加提升副本。
词形松散，像没真处理过切换。
听不出机制，像临场瞎凑。
太书面，像背文档不像讲系统。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They see you know failover plus promoting.
Loose forms — doubts you've done it.
No mechanism — sounds improvised.
Too written — a doc, not your system.
optionDirectness: 抓住动词切换加提升副本动作链。
错在词形：名词当动词用。
错在粒度：只说切，没点备库、提升。
错在语域：书面体太僵。
optionDirectness_en: Nails the verb-switch plus promote chain.
Wrong form: noun used as a verb.
Wrong grain: only switch, no standby/promote.

termDefinitions.meaning: 动词：主库挂了自动切到备库继续服务。名词 failover 指这次切换动作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To fail over is to switch service to a standby when the primary dies; the noun "failover" is that switch.

termDefinitions.meaning: 平时待命的备用副本，主库挂了就顶上来。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A standby replica waits on the side and takes over when the primary fails.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个副本提升成新的主库，让它开始接写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To promote a replica is to make it the new primary so it starts taking writes.

scenario: 系统设计面，面试官问「异步复制的代价是什么」。你想说最终一致性，却卡成 we want to consistency，还把 ACID 念成 half acid。
scenario_en: In a system design round you're asked the cost of async replication. You mean eventual consistency but stall into "we want to consistency" and mispronounce ACID as "half acid."
q: 「读可能读到旧数据，之后才一致」这个点怎么说出口？
q_en: How do you say "reads can be stale, then it becomes consistent later"?
options: we want to consistency, so the data becomes the same eventually, the eventual consistency, half acid...
so it's not consistent right away, the data is a bit old, and then later, later it becomes correct...
The system offers eventual consistency, whereby all replicas asymptotically reach a consistent state.
Replication is async, so reads can be stale briefly, then the replicas converge — eventual consistency.
tradeoff: 术语加机制 vs 卡壳绕圈：stale 加 converge 直接命名代价；we want to consistency 是语法崩加复读，绕半天没落到术语。
why: 搭配是读到 stale 值、之后各副本 converge，代价叫 eventual consistency；consistency 前别接 to，ACID 读 /æsɪd/。
why_en: Reads can be stale briefly, then the replicas converge — that's eventual consistency.
whenOtherWins: 只有对方不熟术语要铺垫时，才用大白话 a bit old；正式答直接说 stale、converge。
options_en: we want to consistency, so the data becomes the same eventually, the eventual consistency, half acid...
so it's not consistent right away, the data is a bit old, and then later, later it becomes correct...
The system offers eventual consistency, whereby all replicas asymptotically reach a consistent state.
Replication is async, so reads can be stale briefly, then the replicas converge — eventual consistency.
optionMeanings: 原话语法崩，ACID 念成 half acid。
只有大白话 a bit old，卡在 later 打转。
学术腔 asymptotically，像念论文。
点明异步、旧读后收敛，术语代价到位。
optionMeanings_en: Names async and converge — term and cost.
optionScenarioImpacts: 语法发音双崩，像没懂一致性模型。
绕圈没落术语，只会大白话。
太学术，像背定义不像讲权衡。
对方懂异步复制代价是最终一致。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Grammar and sound break — doubts the model.
Circles without the term — plain talk only.
Too academic — a definition, not a tradeoff.
They get async cost is eventual consistency.
optionDirectness: 错在语法发音，露怯。
错在粒度：只 a bit old，没点旧读收敛。
错在语域：学术词太书面。
抓住旧读加收敛，命名最终一致。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong grammar and sound — exposes gaps.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写完后副本不立刻一致，读可能拿到旧值，但最终会收敛一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency means replicas aren't instantly in sync — reads may be stale but eventually converge.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读到的是还没同步的旧值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A stale read returns an old value that hasn't synced yet.

termDefinitions.meaning: 各副本最终追平、达到相同状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To converge is for all replicas to catch up to the same state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主库不等副本确认就返回，副本稍后异步追。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Async replication returns before replicas confirm; they catch up afterward.

scenario: 系统设计面，面试官问「单表写不动了怎么办」。你想说按 user ID 分片，却说成 do the sharding to separate the data，没点到分片键。
scenario_en: In a system design round you're asked how to scale writes on one huge table. You mean sharding by user ID but say "do the sharding to separate the data," never naming the shard key.
q: 「按 user ID 分片」这句话怎么说才像做过？
q_en: How do you say "shard by user ID" like you've actually done it?
options: we do the sharding to separate the data, so we split it into some parts by the user, the shards...
We shard the table by user ID, so each shard owns one slice of the key space.
so we break the data into pieces, so each piece has some users, and the pieces sit on different servers...
The dataset shall be horizontally partitioned into shards keyed on the user identifier.
tradeoff: 分片键点名 vs 泛泛拆分：说清按哪个键切才像做过；separate the data 只说了拆，没说按什么键。
why: 动词 shard by user ID 点出分片键，再说各片 owns a slice of the key space 证明懂键空间；别停在没键的 separate the data。
why_en: We shard the table by user ID, so each shard owns one slice of the key space.
whenOtherWins: 只有还没定分片键、只想说「要水平拆」时，split into parts 才够；聊扩写就得点名 shard key。
options_en: we do the sharding to separate the data, so we split it into some parts by the user, the shards...
We shard the table by user ID, so each shard owns one slice of the key space.
so we break the data into pieces, so each piece has some users, and the pieces sit on different servers...
The dataset shall be horizontally partitioned into shards keyed on the user identifier.
optionMeanings: 只说拆数据，没点按什么键分。
按 user ID 分片，键空间点到位。
碎片化大白话，一直打转。
规范腔 partitioned，像念文档。
optionMeanings_en: Says split but names no shard key.
Shard by user ID — the key lands.
optionScenarioImpacts: 没说按什么键切，像没设计过分片。
对方知道你按 user ID 切、每片管一段。
听不出分片键是什么。
太书面，像背规范不像讲方案。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: No shard key — doubts you've designed it.
They see you shard by user ID, one slice each.
The shard key never surfaces.
Too written — a spec, not your plan.
optionDirectness: 错在缺键：说了拆，没点按哪个键。
抓住按键分片加键空间落点。
错在粒度：碎片描述没点键。
错在语域：书面体太僵。
optionDirectness_en: Missing the key: split but no shard key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把大表按某个键横向切成的一片，各自存一段数据、独立扩展。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A shard is one horizontal slice of a table split by a key, holding part of the data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定一行落到哪个分片的字段，比如 user ID。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The shard key is the field that decides which shard a row lands in, e.g. user ID.

termDefinitions.meaning: 所有可能键值的整个范围；每个分片认领其中一段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The key space is the full range of possible keys; each shard owns a slice of it.

scenario: 系统设计面，面试官问「怎么保证一条写不会丢」。你想说要多数副本确认，却绕成 most of the nodes say okay，没干脆点出 quorum。
scenario_en: In a system design round you're asked how a write won't be lost. You mean a majority of replicas must confirm, but circle into "most of the nodes say okay" instead of naming quorum.
q: 「写要过半副本确认才算提交」这句话怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "a write commits only after a majority of replicas confirm"?
options: we need most of the nodes to say okay, the quorum, so the majority, most of them ack, then it's done...
so we wait for enough of the copies to confirm, like enough of them, and then we know it's safe, so...
A write isn't committed until a quorum of replicas acks it, so it survives a node dying.
A write is acknowledged only upon confirmations from a quorum-constituting subset of replicas.
tradeoff: 术语加后果 vs 同义复读：quorum 加抗单点故障一句点名机制和收益；majority、most 把一个意思绕三遍。
why: 搭配是 a quorum of replicas acks 这条写，再点后果能抗单点故障；别把 quorum、majority、most 同义词绕三遍。
why_en: A write isn't committed until a quorum of replicas acks it, so it survives a node dying.
whenOtherWins: 只有对方不熟 quorum 要你先解释时，才铺一句 a majority of the copies；随后仍要落回 quorum。
options_en: we need most of the nodes to say okay, the quorum, so the majority, most of them ack, then it's done...
so we wait for enough of the copies to confirm, like enough of them, and then we know it's safe, so...
A write isn't committed until a quorum of replicas acks it, so it survives a node dying.
A write is acknowledged only upon confirmations from a quorum-constituting subset of replicas.
optionMeanings: 把三个同义词绕着说三遍。
只说 enough copies，卡在重复。
点名 quorum、能抗单点故障，机制到位。
堆砌 subset 术语，像念论文。
optionMeanings_en: Says three synonyms three times over.
optionScenarioImpacts: 同义反复，像在拖时间凑术语。
没点 quorum，抓不住机制。
对方懂过半确认才提交、抗单点故障。
太堆砌，像背定义不像讲保证。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Synonym loop — sounds like stalling.
No quorum — misses the mechanism.
They get quorum-commit survives one failure.
Word-pile — a definition, not a guarantee.
optionDirectness: 错在复读：一个意思说三遍。
错在粒度：只 enough，没点 quorum。
抓住过半确认加抗故障机制。
错在语域：术语堆砌太僵。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong via repetition: one idea thrice.
Nails quorum-acks with the fault-tolerance payoff.
Wrong register: piled terms, too stiff.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让一次读或写生效所需的最少副本数，通常是过半。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the minimum number of replicas that must respond for a read or write to count, usually a majority.

termDefinitions.meaning: 副本确认已收到并写下这条数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To ack is for a replica to confirm it has received and stored the write.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条写被正式定案、不会回滚，对读可见。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To commit a write is to finalize it so it won't roll back and is visible to reads.
